verdict.rationale: mise documents its own locked install mode: commit a lockfile and run `mise install --locked` so every CI job installs the same versions. That is a first-party frozen-lockfile capability. The evidence never says the command fails when mise.toml and mise.lock disagree, so the enforcement behavior the story requires is only implied. Missing for 10: documented failure/exit behavior on manifest–lockfile mismatch, details of what --locked checks, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a platform-engineer, I can enforce a frozen/immutable lockfile mode that fails the install when the manifest and lockfile disagree

citations.quote: For reproducible installs, commit a [lockfile](/dev-tools/mise-lock.html) and run `mise install --locked`.
Commit a lockfile and install with `mise install --locked`. Every job then installs the same versions
